extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering, consisting of 12,247 multiple-choice questions generated from ConceptNet.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by extracting subgraphs from ConceptNet (a source concept and multiple target concepts) and having crowd-workers manually author multiple-choice questions that discriminate between the target concepts. Workers also added distractors and filtered the questions for quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data consists of knowledge base subgraphs extracted from ConceptNet, specifically containing a single source concept and multiple target concepts that share the same semantic relation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers were tasked with authoring multiple-choice questions that mention a source concept and discriminate between target concepts. They were instructed to ensure high language variation. The process also involved crowd-workers filtering questions by quality and adding distractors.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating natural language understanding (NLU) models on commonsense question answering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors filtered ConceptNet triplets by removing general or well-explored relations, concepts longer than four words or not in English, and concepts with low edit distance. They also filtered out generated questions that failed a quality verification step by crowd-workers.

Crowd-workers are asked to author multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate in turn between each of the target concepts.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: 1. We filter triplets with general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or relations that are already well-explored in NLP (e.g., IsA). In total we use 22 relations. 2. We filter triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English. 3. We filter triplets where the edit distance between c1 and c2 is too low. [...] Each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used. This processes filters out 15% of the questions.
